Thanks Mina — attaching the network diagram and the on-prem inventory you asked for. A few quick notes from our side: 

- We currently have a /16 allocated for our VPCs but can carve a /20 for Redwood peering.
- The on-prem gateway runs NAT for outbound; we will need to confirm static egress IPs for the private endpoints.
- HSM/KMS will be managed by our security team; they prefer TLS mutual auth to the Redwood control-plane endpoints.

See attachments: luminex_network_diagram_v2.pdf, onprem_server_inventory.xlsx.

We can do the preflight call tomorrow at 10am PT if that works for your engineering team.

—Marco
Director, Infrastructure
Luminex Analytics

Hi Marco —

Thanks again for the time earlier. To keep momentum for the Private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints + on-prem package) we need the following before the preflight: 

1) High-level network diagram showing VPC CIDRs, on-prem subnets, and firewalls (PDF)
2) On-prem server inventory with OS versions and outbound IPs (Excel)
3) Preferred time window for installing the on-prem package (2–3 hour window)
4) Contacts for security/KMS owners for mutual-auth discussion

If you can send the artifacts and confirm availability for a 60-minute call tomorrow, we’ll prepare the runbook and cutover checklist.

Cheers,
Mina
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Action items from our side before the 10am PT call: 
- Ben: run a quick CIDR compatibility check and list candidate /20s we can peer into. (Ben, adding you for the checklist)
- Kimberly: prepare the control-plane TLS mTLS requirements and the KMS integration questions.
- I will draft the cutover checklist and a proposed rollback plan.

Please confirm the 10:00–11:00 PT window and whether the on-prem team can provide static egress IPs or if we should plan for NAT traversal during installation.

Also attaching a short vpc-cidr-proposal.txt with what we've seen work in similar customers (you'll get that on the call).

Thanks — Mina

Quick notes after scanning the diagram/inventory: 

- Luminex /16 is fine; proposed peering candidate ranges (non-overlapping): 10.240.0.0/20, 10.241.0.0/20, 10.242.0.0/20. I will validate routing table limits and BGP feasibility on the call.
- On-prem server OS mix looks standard (RHEL 8, Ubuntu 20.04, Windows Server 2019). No kernel-level blockers for the Redwood appliance.
- For the on-prem package install: recommend scheduling 2-hour maintenance window, with a 30-minute smoke test and 1-hour rollback buffer.

I marked a few lines in the inventory where we should request fixed outbound IPs (rows 14, 21, 35).

Ben

Thanks all — 10am PT worked well. Quick recap and confirmations from our side: 

- We will reserve 10.241.0.0/20 for the peering; ops confirmed the CIDR is free.
- On-prem will provide the static egress IPs for the installer by next Monday (2025-03-31).
- Security would like the TLS mutual-auth cert exchange to happen out-of-band; they prefer a signed CSR to our key-management team.

Next steps: 
1) Redwood to create the runbook and share the Doc (link in thread) — Mina, Ben & Kim will own sections.
2) Luminex to produce the signed CSR and the fixed egress IP list.
3) Schedule the install for week of Apr 7; tentative 2hr maintenance window.

Appreciate the quick cadence — looking forward to the install.

—Marco
